rationale: A wins because it understands the difference between a story and an unsupported leap. Its best line, "Faire calls it interest-free. Someone is still paying for the risk," turns a disclosed hole into a reportable question. B has useful shapes, especially the brand-side angle, but "no bank required" and "Faire absorbs all the default risk" turn unknowns into facts. That is how a decent angle becomes a correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: Misses the clean brand-side protagonist B found: "brands are paid upfront while retailers pay later" could support a distinct wholesale-terms angle, not just Faire-risk angles.
Some overlap among "quietly becomes a lender," "becomes a bank," and "Someone is still paying for the risk"; the lenses are different, but three of four circle the same credit-risk machinery.
"cash flow, not demand" overstates the fact. The update says cash flow is the top barrier to ordering; it does not prove demand is healthy or secondary.
"quietly becomes a lender" adds color the update does not supply. Fine as a draft headline, but it needs tightening before a real pitch.
gaps_in_B: "no bank required" is invented. The update says Faire underwrites using order history; it does not say there is no bank, facility, partner, insurer, or other capital structure behind it.
"Faire isn't using a credit bureau" and "purchase frequency" are unsupported specifics. Order history is in the facts; credit-bureau exclusion and model inputs are not.
"Faire absorbs all the default risk" overclaims. The facts show a timing gap and undisclosed terms, not that Faire absorbs all losses with no partner or protection.
The next step is wrong: "meanest-editor" critiques drafts. This set needs journalist-fit-check and fact cleanup before anyone writes a pitch.
